reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the finding correctly proposes no redline and no comment; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs, so nothing invalid or directionally wrong is introduced.

The cited § 11.3 text supports the rationale: it is an AUP/content-warranty investigation and remedy provision (restrict access, require removal, terminate) with an attempted-notice undertaking, not a usage/records audit binding the Customer. It confers no access to Customer premises, systems, books or records, no remote access, and no audit cost or cooperation burden, so there is nothing to parametrize with frequency/notice/cost/no-system-access limits.

Evidence of absence is specific and checkable (no 'audit', 'inspect', 'verify', 'monitor', 'premises' hits; 'records' only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out; the plausible host sections § 4.1, § 4.2, § 11.5, § 12.1, § 13.2 and §§ 14.1–14.20 reviewed), which adequately rebuts the failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check as an artifact of absence rather than a material gap.

Declining to treat this as 'missing' is correct: inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour that it does not currently hold, contrary to the rule's protective purpose and the instruction not to flag terms benefiting our party.

The uncapped frequency and best-efforts notice in § 11.3 are appropriately handled as a noted residual observation (and would in any event belong to an acceptable-use/suspension rule rather than AUDIT), avoiding double-flagging of the same commercial term.
